rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Dawn: Assigning roles 2 Day: Managing your village and preparing the offerings 3 Dusk: End of the round 4 Favor Bonuses 5 End Game Scoring Dawn: Assigning roles In secret, all players assign a role to each of the 5 artisans in their hand. Assign 1 resident to your village to create offerings with beneficial effects. Send 2 travelers to the village on your left. Keep 2 craftsmen, who will produce items during the next phase. THE RESIDENT ARTISAN Choose which artisan will be your resident. Place this card face down in an EMPTY workshop slot of your village. At any point during the dawn or day phase, you may EMPTY A WORKSHOP by removing the Artisan card from it. There are two possible cases: If there's no offering token on this artisan card, place it on the discard pile. You do not gain any favor points or items. If there is an offering token on this artisan card, place it under your palace gate and the offering token next to your village. This artisan's favor points will count toward your score at the end of the game. THE TRAVELER ARTISANS Choose your 2 traveler artisans and place them face down to your left, between your village and that of your neighbor. They will take these cards in their hand at the start of the next round. THE CRAFTSMAN ARTISANS Choose your 2 craftsman artisans and keep them in your hand. In the next phase, you will discard them to gain the items they produce (indicated in the lantern). FINAL ROUND The dawn phase works differently in the final round. All players must assign 1 resident, 4 craftsmen, and 0 travelers. Day: Managing your village and preparing the offerings Discard 2 identical items take 1 other item of your choice from the general supply. Prepare the offering Prepare the offering of 1 of the artisans in your village. Discard all of the items the artisan requires from your personal supply, and place an offering token on the artisan's card. Send an artisan to the palace If an artisan card from one of your workshops contains an offering token, you may place the card under your palace gate and the offering token next to your village. The favors of this artisan will be counted toward your score at the end of the game. Dusk: End of the round In Order: Check to see if your village contains artisans with an hour glass icon. If so, their effect triggers now. From the second round onward, take 1 objective token you fulfill the objective of the day. At the very end of this phase, check your personal supply. You cannot have more than 7 items. If you have more, discard the items of your choice. Favor Bonuses Regardless of the phase, each time you reach or cross a 10-Favor threshold thanks to the effects of the artisans in your workshops (not under palace), immediately gain 2 Items of your choice: the same or different. This can cause you to go over 7 item and need to discard if it happens during dusk. End Game Scoring Score a number of favor points based on the number of objective tokens you’ve gained, reference table Add the total value of the favor tokens you gained throughout the game, thanks to the effects of your artisans. Add the total amount of favor points from the artisan cards you placed under your palace gate.

---

Put down a card which may trigger an effect. Discard 2 other cards and get the resources shown (you need them to play other cards).  All of that is fine and I even liked the way you place the cards around your castle, but man, this is just random. If you don't get the right cards, you don't do much. [Rating: 5/10] I've found my plays both interesting and frustrating - completing the goals and getting cards that work together are all down to luck of the draw and if playing with other players, they can pass you cards that don't help even further limiting your chances of getting what you want...some room for creative play but if you can't get the cards at the right time...

[Rating: 5/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  BGA - 2 plays. Seems to try to do a little too much for a short tableau builder and engine builder. Beautiful art although theme seems pretty tacked on. Can be very annoying when you don't get the card you need for several turns and then it is too late once you do have access.

[Rating: 5/10] Kinda boring... A Tableau builder that lacks unique features and appeal. Feels a little "on rails" and doesn't make me want to replay it.

[Rating: 5/10] It's a card-based engine-builder.  Absolutely no theme, the art is "eh", and pretty much everything about it is "eh".  Very restrictive (there's 12 rounds, and 1 goal on each of Days 2-11), so careful planning and flipluck management is required to do well, but...it never felt like there were any fun "moments" or great moves.  It was just "Yep, that worked, what's next" or "Well, that didn't work."

[Rating: 5/10] Multi-use cards. Players place card in different locations. Some of the cards need to be place in specific areas (top, left, right, bottom) of your tableau.  Other cards you don't want in your tableau can be passed to your opponents.  You use the cards to generate resources and  use those resources to craft items.  Some cards provide you with points for generating certain resources.  If you move your card (villager) to your gate to have them score you points. Players with the most points wins.

[Rating: 5/10] Initial Impressions: The card sequencing of leveraging your somewhat temporary powers is interesting in the middle and late game, but early game I feel like there is very little control, which matters a lot because the end of round objectives is potentially such a big source of points, so missing one or two early is a big deal. I didn't dislike the objectives as much as I expected or generally do, since it is so important I could basically just treat it as a soft constraint, but I'd still prefer a game focused on the cards rather than these arbitrary objectives.
